name: William Creek
reason: Town with its own Wikivoyage page and flindersandoutback.com.au town page; the William Creek Hotel pub is a named stop on the Oodnadatta Track (rule 1, 2)
objection: Tiny settlement, mainly a pub and airstrip; the visit is a meal and a photo

name: Cadney Homestead
reason: Roadhouse/business; Wikivoyage mentions it as an oasis stop only (rule 2: shop/restaurant)
objection: Wikivoyage calls it a nice surprise on the highway and it is the gateway to the Painted Desert

name: Mungerannie
reason: Outback pub and roadhouse on the Birdsville Track known for its memorabilia, a quirky roadside icon; only one counted source (flindersandoutback region page)
objection: It is a roadhouse and accommodation business and the source gives little to see

name: Oodnadatta Track
reason: Wikivoyage itinerary page gives the 617 km track its own article with sidings, mound springs and Lake Eyre South; an obvious outback draw (rule 1)
objection: A long linear feature, its stops are already separate candidates, and a pin on a line is arbitrary

name: Strzelecki Track
reason: Wikivoyage has its own article for the track, a remote route to Innamincka; one counted source and a drive, not a place to stop (rule 1,3)
objection: Equivalent to the Oodnadatta Track as a named outback route; against: remote, gravel and mostly a transit road

name: Anne Beadell Highway
reason: Remote 4WD desert route needing permits, mentioned in passing on the Stuart Highway page; no visitor stop (rule 2)
objection: A famous outback track; against: a one-line mention and most of it lies in another state

name: Painted Desert (South Australia)
reason: Wikivoyage Stuart Highway names the Painted Desert reached by AWD track from Cadney; coloured hills visitors go to, one source (rule 1)
objection: Real scenic draw; against: one passing mention, rough access, usually seen via tours or flights

name: Faye's Underground Home
reason: Wikivoyage Coober Pedy See listing: tour of a hand-dug underground home, open daily except Sunday, $5 (rule 2)
objection: Small family attraction; one counted source

name: Old Timers Mine
reason: Wikivoyage See listing: self-guided tour of a 1916 mine and underground homes, a signature Coober Pedy visit (rule 2)
objection: Wikivoyage link is marked dead; only one source

name: Tom's Working Opal Mine
reason: Wikivoyage calls it the pick of the working mines on Stuart Highway, but it is a tour operator; near-duplicate of the other mine visits
objection: It is a tour operator listing; for: a distinct working mine visit

name: Big Winch
reason: Wikivoyage See listing: lookout in the middle of Coober Pedy over the opal fields; a landmark Big Thing (rule 2,3)
objection: Short stop

name: Umoona Opal Mine and Museum
reason: southaustralia.com region page names it; underground mine, museum and dugout, a main Coober Pedy attraction (rule 2)
objection: Commercial business with accommodation; source is a region page

name: Saint Elijah the Prophet Serbian Orthodox Church
reason: Wikivoyage: church bored out of solid rock with a beautifully ornamented interior, a must see (church rule: interior named)
objection: Active church, may be restricted by services

name: Catholic Catacomb Church
reason: Wikivoyage names the Catholic church as a significant site but less intricate than the Serbian one; one source (church rule)
objection: For: underground interior a guide mentions; against: lesser than the Serbian church

name: Dingo Fence at Coober Pedy
reason: Wikivoyage Stuart Highway suggests a dirt-road trip 10 km to the Dingo Fence; landmark, one source
objection: For: iconic structure; against: a fence beside a road, 10 minute stop

name: Coober Pedy Mail Run
reason: Tour/vehicle operator, not a place (COVERAGE: a spot is a place); link is dead
objection: A famous outback experience; against: an operator ride

name: Moon Plain
reason: southaustralia.com region page names the lunar-like plain and film location south of Coober Pedy; one counted source and a roadside look
objection: For: second-tier icon; against: a plain visited from a road, mostly seen by tour

name: Coober Pedy opal noodling fields
reason: An activity, not a distinct place; fossicking is covered by Coober Pedy tours and the mines (rule 3)
objection: Visitors do noodle; against: no single place or named site

name: Karkaroo (Andamooka Plesiosaur)
reason: Cannot confirm a public display place or visitor source describing where to see it (rule 1,2)
objection: Opalised fossil is a genuine curiosity

name: Lake Cadibarrawirracanna
reason: Remote salt lake with a passing mention only, no visitor facilities or description (rule 1,2)
objection: A large lake in the Arckaringa area

name: Woomera Missile Park
reason: Wikivoyage See listing: free open-air display of missiles and rockets in the town centre, with the Heritage Centre beside it (rule 2)
objection: Short stop of about 30 minutes

name: Woomera Heritage Centre
reason: Wikivoyage lists the Rocket Range Museum in the visitors' centre, about an hour, $6 (rule 2)
objection: Small museum; the History Museum next door may be a near duplicate

name: Woomera Obelisk
reason: Minor Australia Day monument beside the theatre (rule 3: minor memorial)
objection: Wikivoyage lists it

name: Deep Station 41
reason: One-line Wikivoyage mention of a former tracking facility 25 km south on range land; no visitor access or description (rule 2)
objection: Historic space-tracking site

name: Breen Park Bird Reserve
reason: Wikivoyage lists it with no description; local park in Woomera (rule 1,3)
objection: Wikivoyage names it

name: Spud's Roadhouse
reason: Roadhouse (restaurant/motel) at Pimba (rule 2)
objection: Quirky outback icon founded 1969 per Wikivoyage

name: Olympic Dam mine tour
reason: Operator tour of a mine (not a spot); the place is Roxby Downs/Olympic Dam, whose access is by booked tour only
objection: Large underground mine, a rare tourist tour

name: Roxby Downs Arid Recovery Reserve
reason: Fenced conservation reserve near Roxby Downs listed by flindersandoutback region page; open via tours, one source
objection: For: unique wildlife; against: access by tour only

name: Lake Torrens National Park
reason: Listed on flindersandoutback national parks page; huge salt lake park with no facilities and difficult access, one source
objection: For: a national park; against: remote and mostly inaccessible

name: Lake Gairdner National Park
reason: Wikivoyage Stuart Highway describes the third largest salt lake in Australia, used for speed records, with a national park beside the highway (rule 1)
objection: Access is hard to find, station-crossing and 4WD

name: Lake Hart
reason: southaustralia.com region page names the pink salt lake beside the Stuart Highway; a roadside stop travellers photograph
objection: Short roadside stop and sparse description

name: Marree Hotel
reason: Pub and accommodation business (rule 2)
objection: 1883 heritage building per Wikivoyage

name: Marree Mosque
reason: Wikivoyage See listing: recreation of Australia's first mosque built by Afghan cameleers (rule 2)
objection: Only a replica, short stop, mud-brick ruins

name: Marree Camel Cup
reason: Annual event, not a permanent place (rule 4)
objection: Famous event

name: Lake Eyre South
reason: Wikivoyage Oodnadatta Track side trip (3 km return) to Lake Eyre South; near-duplicate of Kati Thanda-Lake Eyre National Park (rule 3)
objection: For: easy roadside look at the lake; against: usually a dry salt flat and part of the larger lake

name: Anna Creek Painted Hills
reason: Seen by scenic flight only per source; a flight, not a place to visit (COVERAGE: spot is a place)
objection: Colourful hills

name: Curdimurka Siding
reason: Wikivoyage: preserved Ghan siding showing how settlers lived, one of the interesting sidings on the track (rule 2)
objection: Ruins and a sign, 20-minute stop

name: The Bubbler and Blanche Cup
reason: Wikivoyage Oodnadatta Track: the two best-known mound springs, a worthwhile diversion (rule 1,2)
objection: Overlaps Wabma Kadarbu Mound Springs Conservation Park

name: Wabma Kadarbu Mound Springs Conservation Park
reason: duplicate of The Bubbler and Blanche Cup (the park holds those springs; kept as one)
objection: Official park, could be the better kept entry
